chapter: Touring, recording and Fletcher's band in the 1940s
title: The October 1940 Okeh session: personnel and 'Smooth Sailing'
summary: Going through the discography, they identify the sidemen on the October 23, 1940 New York Okeh date, including Sir Charles Thompson who wrote 'Smooth Sailing', and Hammond's love of blues.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Okay. I've got some recording lists here in 1940. This would be for you, and this would have been some on Okeh -- let's see -- Chicago, May 8, 1940.
Okay. Now here's one date in 1940 -- October 23, 1940 in New York for Okeh.
Okay. And you've got on here Emmett Berry, Nat Bates, Harold Johnson, Leo Williams, Archie Brown, Howard Johnson, C.Q. Price.
Leonard Talley was on baritone saxophone. Yes.
Debo Mills, and -- here, listen -- Sir Charles Thompson.
Sir Charles is a great organist.
He wrote a tune called 'Smooth Sailing' which we recorded. Man, that was the jumpiest thing, and he made the arrangement for me.
It's listed here. There are four tracks you have, or you don't -- let's see -- 'You Don't Mean No Good.' That must be --
That's the one Danny Bo sang to his
wife. That's the blues. John Hammond was a blues fiend, as you know.
He loved Bessie and Clara Smith.
He thought that they were the greatest blues singers that ever lived.
And you have "Smooth Sailing," "Ain't Misbehaving," and "I'll Always Be In Love With You."
Yeah. So those were the four dates there.
That's the time that we were (Inaudible) -- just discussing.
